articles.title: Lawyer Shot Dead Inside District Panchayat Office in Rampur; Clerk Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Rampur (Uttar Pradesh): A 45-year-old lawyer, Farooq Ahmed Khan, was shot dead in broad daylight inside the District Panchayat office in Rampur on February 11, 2026, triggering outrage among the local legal community.

body.html:
Rampur (Uttar Pradesh): A 45-year-old lawyer, Farooq Ahmed Khan, was shot dead in broad daylight inside the District Panchayat office in Rampur on February 11, 2026, triggering outrage among the local legal community.

According to police, the incident stemmed from a dispute between two clerks. Farooq’s wife, Gausia, who works as a clerk in the District Panchayat office, reportedly had a heated argument earlier in the day with fellow clerk Asgar Ali, a resident of Tahawwur village under Patwai police station limits.

Following the altercation, Gausia called her husband to the office. Around 1 pm, Advocate Farooq reached the premises and went to Asgar Ali’s cabin to confront him. CCTV footage and eyewitness accounts suggest that the verbal exchange escalated, and Farooq allegedly slapped Asgar, leading to a physical scuffle.

During the confrontation, Asgar Ali allegedly pulled out his licensed revolver and fired multiple shots. Farooq sustained two bullet injuries to the chest and was rushed to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Gausia was also allegedly assaulted with the butt of the weapon and sustained injuries.

Police said the accused clerk also suffered a gunshot wound, suspected to be self-inflicted, allegedly to support a claim of self-defence.

The incident led to chaos at the district hospital, where family members of the deceased created a ruckus in the emergency ward. Lawyers in Rampur staged protests, alleging deteriorating law and order and demanding stronger protection measures for advocates, including a Lawyers’ Protection Act.

Rampur Superintendent of Police Vidya Sagar Mishra, Additional SP Anurag Singh and District Magistrate Ajay Kumar Dwivedi reached the hospital to pacify the agitated family.

Police have arrested Asgar Ali, who is currently under medical supervision while in custody. An FIR has been registered under Section 103 (Murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The body has been sent for post-mortem examination, and further legal action will be taken based on the complaint filed by the victim’s family.

Authorities said a detailed investigation is underway to ascertain the full sequence of events.

articles.title: Bareilly Police Crack 8-Year-Old Murder While Solving Teen Girl Case; Two Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bareilly (Uttar Pradesh): Police in Bareilly have arrested two accused and claimed to have solved two murder cases — one dating back eight years and another involving the killing of a 16-year-old girl about 1.25 years ago.

body.html:
Bareilly (Uttar Pradesh): Police in Bareilly have arrested two accused and claimed to have solved two murder cases — one dating back eight years and another involving the killing of a 16-year-old girl about 1.25 years ago.

Kyoldia police station registered a missing complaint on January 8, 2025, after a villager reported that his teenage daughter had disappeared. A case was initially filed under Crime No. 009/2025, Section 137(2) IPC.

In September 2025, police recovered a braided scalp, clothes and skeletal remains from a sugarcane field near the Kailash River. DNA testing confirmed that the remains belonged to the missing girl. Subsequently, Sections 103(1)/238 IPC were added to the case.

Arrest of Accused

During investigation, mobile call detail records (CDR) revealed suspicious activity by Salim Hussain (22), a resident of the same village. He had frequent conversations with the girl and his location matched the crime scene on the night of the incident.

After obtaining court permission, police initiated proceedings for a polygraph test. Upon receiving notice, Salim allegedly absconded. Further inquiry revealed that he worked at a clinic in Bhaua Bazaar with Asim alias Amit alias “Dr. Bengali,” a native of West Bengal.

On February 11, police apprehended both accused at Bauria Cut near Bhaua Bazaar while they were allegedly preparing to flee to West Bengal.

Confession and Link to 2017 Murder

During interrogation, Salim allegedly confessed to calling the teenager out at night, taking her to a sugarcane field and strangling her. He then dumped the body and threw his mobile phone into the river. Police said he was in a relationship with the girl.

Meanwhile, co-accused Asim alias Dr. Bengali allegedly confessed to the 2017 murder of his wife, Rajni. Police claim that due to marital disputes, he, along with Salim, strangled her on the banks of the Kailash River and buried the body. A separate case has been registered at Bhuta police station in this regard.

Criminal Background

Police stated that Salim Hussain has a criminal history, including cases of robbery, attempt to murder and violations under the Arms Act, and is now accused in two murder cases.

Asim alias Amit alias Dr. Bengali had earlier been named in kidnapping and POCSO Act cases and now faces charges of murdering his wife.

SP North Mukesh Kumar Mishra said that joint teams of surveillance, cyber cell and SOG solved the case based on technical evidence. Legal proceedings are underway, and police are preparing to file charge sheets in both murder cases. Further investigation into other possible aspects is ongoing.

articles.title: Uproar in Bhadohi After Accused Brought to Court in Handcuffs; Citizens Cite Supreme Court Guideline
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bhadohi (Uttar Pradesh): Tension prevailed in Bhadohi district after police escorted several accused to the court premises in handcuffs for arraignment, triggering objections from local residents and rights activists.

body.html:
Bhadohi (Uttar Pradesh): Tension prevailed in Bhadohi district after police escorted several accused to the court premises in handcuffs for arraignment, triggering objections from local residents and rights activists.

Eyewitnesses claimed that the accused were visibly handcuffed in public view, prompting protests. Citizens argued that, as per guidelines issued by the Supreme Court and the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), accused persons should not be handcuffed in public or within court premises without specific and recorded reasons.

Protesters have demanded a formal inquiry into the incident and action against the officers responsible. They stated that handcuffing without clear justification violates established legal norms and human rights principles.

Police sources, however, maintained that the decision was taken strictly for security reasons. According to officials, the accused are facing serious charges and there was apprehension that they might attempt to flee. Police also pointed out that about a month ago, an accused had escaped from the court premises during a hearing, and strict precautions were being taken to prevent a repeat incident.

Despite the security explanation, residents stressed that there are clear restrictions on the use of handcuffs inside court premises, which led to the public outcry.

The incident has sparked a wider debate in the district over balancing security concerns with legal safeguards. It remains to be seen what action higher authorities will take following the demands for a transparent investigation.

articles.title: ‘Shot for Publicity?’ Deoband Jail Visit Sparks Fresh Storm Over UP’s ‘Half-Encounter’ Claims
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Deoband (Uttar Pradesh): Amid sharp observations by the Allahabad High Court on so-called “half-encounters” in Uttar Pradesh, Deoband Court ACGM Parvinder Singh personally visited Deoband jail and interrogated prisoners who were injured in recent police encounters.

body.html:
Deoband (Uttar Pradesh): Amid sharp observations by the Allahabad High Court on so-called “half-encounters” in Uttar Pradesh, Deoband Court ACGM Parvinder Singh personally visited Deoband jail and interrogated prisoners who were injured in recent police encounters.

During the visit, injured inmates were lined up and questioned about the circumstances in which they were shot. A video of the interaction has surfaced, showing the ACGM recording statements.

One prisoner alleged that he was picked up by police while on his way to attend a court hearing. “We had a hearing in Saharanpur and were coming from Baghpat. As soon as we reached Shamli Park, police picked us up and took us to the police station. There, I was given electric shocks and pressured to confess. Later in the evening, they took us to a forest, brought my bike from the police station and shot me in the leg,” he claimed.

When asked where he was shot, the prisoner replied, “Below the leg.” He further alleged that they were made to lie on the ground, their legs lowered, a cloth placed over them, and then shot from about eight inches above. A second injured youth indicated that a similar incident had happened to him.

Allahabad High Court’s Strong Remarks

On January 30, the Allahabad High Court expressed serious displeasure over alleged “half-encounter” practices by the UP Police. The bench led by Justice Arun Kumar Deswal observed that in several cases, accused persons were being shot below the knee allegedly for publicity, praise, early promotions and social media attention.

The court made it clear that awarding punishment is the judiciary’s role, not the police’s. “India is a democratic country governed by the Constitution, not by personal opinion,” the court observed while granting bail in a case.

The High Court warned that failure to follow Supreme Court guidelines laid down in the PUCL vs State of Maharashtra (2014) judgment could lead to contempt proceedings. It stated that district SPs, SSPs and Commissioners of Police could be held personally liable if due procedure is not followed.

Six Key Guidelines Issued by the High Court
FIR and Independent Investigation:
In cases where the accused is seriously injured in an encounter, an FIR must be registered. The investigation should be conducted by an independent team, senior in rank to the officer involved.

Naming of Police Personnel:
Individual names of policemen need not be mentioned in the FIR; the team (STF or local police) may be cited.

Medical Treatment and Statement:
The injured accused must receive immediate medical treatment. After being declared fit, their statement should be recorded by a magistrate or medical officer.

Report to Competent Court:
After completion of investigation, a report must be submitted to the competent court, following Supreme Court procedures.

Ban on Immediate Promotions/Awards:
No out-of-turn promotions or gallantry awards should be granted immediately after an encounter. Any recognition must follow a proper committee inquiry establishing genuine bravery.

Right of Victim’s Family to Complain:
If the family believes the investigation was unfair, they can approach the Sessions Judge. The matter may be escalated to the High Court, and contempt proceedings may be initiated against the concerned SP/SSP.

The jail inspection by ACGM Parvinder Singh comes within a week of the High Court’s remarks, intensifying scrutiny over alleged encounter practices in the state. Police authorities have yet to issue a detailed public response to the latest allegations.

articles.title: Anganwadi Teacher Booked After Child Allegedly Loses Eye Due to Severe Beating in Rajanna Siricilla
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Rajanna Siricilla (Telangana): An Anganwadi teacher has been booked after a child allegedly suffered grievous injuries, including loss of vision in one eye, following a severe beating at an Anganwadi centre in Venkataapur village of Ellareddipet mandal.

body.html:
Rajanna Siricilla (Telangana): An Anganwadi teacher has been booked after a child allegedly suffered grievous injuries, including loss of vision in one eye, following a severe beating at an Anganwadi centre in Venkataapur village of Ellareddipet mandal.

The child, identified as Vidvansh, is the son of Kompelli Lakshmi and Vijay Kumar. The couple had left him at the local Anganwadi centre while they went to work.

According to the family, Anganwadi teacher Rani later called them, stating that the child had developed a fever and asked them to take him home. However, when the parents rushed to the centre, they found serious injuries on the child’s eye and hands.

The boy was immediately shifted to a hospital for treatment. Doctors reportedly confirmed severe damage to one eye.

Based on a complaint lodged by the child’s father, police have registered a case against the Anganwadi teacher and initiated an investigation into the incident.

Authorities are examining the circumstances under which the injuries occurred.

articles.title: Seattle to Pay $29 Million to Family of Andhra Student Jahnavi Kandula Killed by Speeding Police Car
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Seattle has agreed to pay at least $29 million (approximately ₹262 crore) in compensation to the family of Jahnavi (Jaahnavi) Kandula, a 23-year-old engineering student from Andhra Pradesh who was killed in January 2023 after being struck by a speeding Seattle Police Department (SPD)...

body.html:
Seattle has agreed to pay at least $29 million (approximately ₹262 crore) in compensation to the family of Jahnavi (Jaahnavi) Kandula, a 23-year-old engineering student from Andhra Pradesh who was killed in January 2023 after being struck by a speeding Seattle Police Department (SPD) patrol vehicle.

Fatal Crash in 2023:
Jahnavi, a native of Kurnool district, had moved to the United States in 2021 to pursue a master’s degree at Northeastern University’s South Lake Union campus. On the evening of January 23, 2023, she was crossing Dexter Avenue at Thomas Street in Seattle when she was hit by a police vehicle driven by SPD officer Kevin Dave.

According to official findings, the speed limit at the location was about 40 kmph (25 mph), but Dave was travelling at 74 mph (approximately 119 kmph). The impact reportedly threw Jahnavi nearly 100 feet, and she died at the scene.

Her parents, Vijaya Laksmi Gundapuneedi and Sreekanth Kandula, later filed a wrongful death lawsuit in King County Superior Court seeking $110 million, along with an additional $11,000 in reference to controversial remarks made after her death.

Controversial Remarks and Officer Action:
Body camera footage later revealed that SPD officer Daniel Auderer, then vice chairman of the Seattle Police Officers Guild, joked about Jahnavi’s death while discussing the case. He was heard saying, “Just write a check. $11,000. She was 26 anyway. She had limited value,” followed by laughter. The remarks triggered outrage both in India and the United States.

Auderer was fired in July 2024 by interim police chief Sue Rahr. He has since filed a $25 million wrongful termination claim against the city, which is pending in court.

Officer Kevin Dave was terminated in January 2025 after the Office of Police Accountability concluded that he failed to drive with “due regard for the safety of all persons.” The report also noted that Dave had been involved in a prior preventable collision and did not have a valid Washington driver’s licence at the time of the crash. Before joining SPD in 2019, Dave had been dismissed from the Tucson Police Department in 2013 following multiple disciplinary investigations.

Legal and Administrative Outcome:
The Seattle City Attorney’s Office confirmed last week that a settlement had been reached with the Kandula family. City Attorney Erika Evans stated, “Jaahnavi Kandula’s death was heartbreaking, and the city hopes this financial settlement brings some sense of closure to the Kandula family. Her life mattered — to her family, her friends and to our community.”

The settlement totals at least $29 million, plus at least $11,000, according to sources familiar with the agreement.

King County Prosecutor Leesa Manion declined to file felony charges against Kevin Dave. Seattle City Attorney Ann Davison instead issued him a negligent driving citation carrying a $5,000 fine.

In response to public outrage, the Seattle Police Department introduced revised emergency driving policies in November 2024, directing officers to drive no faster than reasonably necessary and within the limits of their skill and training.

The Kandula family’s response to the settlement is awaited.

articles.title: House Arrest Fails to Stop Threat: Pinky Chaudhary Says Team Has Already Reached Kotdwar
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Kotdwar/Ghaziabad: Pinky Chaudhary, who had publicly announced plans to “remove Deepak’s mullah-ness”, has been placed under house arrest in Ghaziabad by the Uttar Pradesh and Haryana Police.

body.html:
Kotdwar/Ghaziabad: Pinky Chaudhary, who had publicly announced plans to “remove Deepak’s mullah-ness”, has been placed under house arrest in Ghaziabad by the Uttar Pradesh and Haryana Police.

Despite police action, Pinky released a video statement in the presence of security personnel, claiming that his team had already left for Kotdwar. In the video, he asserted that Deepak’s “mullah-ness” would be removed today as planned.

Authorities are monitoring the situation closely.

articles.title: Hindu Raksha Dal Leader Calls for Kotdwar March Over ‘Mohammad Deepak’ Row; Police Issue Warning
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Kotdwar (Uttarakhand): A video of Bhupendra alias Pinky Chaudhary, president of the Hindu Raksha Dal in Ghaziabad, has gone viral in which he calls for a march to Kotdwar on February 12 at 3 pm, targeting a local gym owner over an ongoing controversy.

body.html:
Kotdwar (Uttarakhand): A video of Bhupendra alias Pinky Chaudhary, president of the Hindu Raksha Dal in Ghaziabad, has gone viral in which he calls for a march to Kotdwar on February 12 at 3 pm, targeting a local gym owner over an ongoing controversy.

In the video, Pinky Chaudhary, seen wearing saffron robes, refers to Uttarakhand as “Devbhoomi” and says it is inappropriate for such “demons” to live there. He announces that his team, along with workers from other districts including “Lalit Bhai and others,” will reach Kotdwar in full force. He ends the video with slogans of “Jai Shri Ram” and urges supporters to gather in large numbers.

Chaudhary alleges that a man named Deepak Rawat has changed his name to “Mohammad Deepak” and is harassing “Hindu brothers” by supporting “mullahs.” He states that members of the Hindu Raksha Dal will assemble outside Deepak’s gym and “expose his mullah-like nature” and teach him a “lesson.”

The controversy traces back to a recent dispute in Kotdwar involving the shop of an elderly Muslim man known locally as “Baba.” Some Hindu organisations objected to the use of the name “Baba,” associating it with a Hindu religious identity, and demanded a change. Deepak reportedly came out in support of the elderly man and publicly referred to himself as “Mohammad Deepak,” after which he came under the scrutiny of certain groups.

Reacting to the viral video, CO Kotdwar Niharika Semwal issued a clear warning. “You are welcome to come, but if you spoil the atmosphere of Kotdwar, we will take action,” she said, indicating that police are monitoring the situation closely.

Security arrangements are expected to be tightened in view of the announced march. Authorities have urged residents to maintain peace and harmony.

articles.title: Love Affair Between Would-Be Son-in-Law and Mother-in-Law Ends in Dispute; Complaint Dismissed
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Aligarh (Uttar Pradesh): A bizarre case involving a former would-be son-in-law and his would-be mother-in-law has resurfaced after the man alleged that the woman fled with cash and jewellery nearly ten months after the two began living together.

body.html:
Aligarh (Uttar Pradesh): A bizarre case involving a former would-be son-in-law and his would-be mother-in-law has resurfaced after the man alleged that the woman fled with cash and jewellery nearly ten months after the two began living together.

Rahul Kumar, a resident of Machhariya Nagla village under Dadon police station, was scheduled to marry in April 2025 in Manoharpur village under Madrak police station limits. During the engagement period, Rahul began speaking frequently on the phone with his would-be mother-in-law, Sapna Devi. Over time, their conversations reportedly turned into a romantic relationship.

According to Rahul and police sources, about 12 days before the scheduled marriage, Sapna Devi left her husband and family and began living with Rahul. Following a complaint by her husband, police conducted raids in several states, including Bihar. The couple later appeared at Dadon police station and were subsequently called to Madrak police station, where both admitted to living together and submitted written statements stating that they wished to stay together. After recording their consent, police allowed them to leave.

Nearly ten months later, on February 11, Rahul reached Dadon police station with a fresh complaint. He alleged that he had been living in a district of Bihar, earning a livelihood by selling clothes through hawking. According to him, on February 6, Sapna Devi left him and fled with her brother-in-law, taking ₹2 lakh in cash and jewellery.

Rahul submitted a written complaint at the police station. However, police officials stated that since the alleged incident occurred outside their jurisdiction, no action would be taken at Dadon police station.

The matter has once again drawn attention due to its unusual sequence of events.

articles.title: Drunk Policeman Runs Over 22-Year-Old Girl in Ambala, Massive Uproar After Incident
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Ambala (Haryana): A 22-year-old woman was killed in a tragic road accident near the Kali Paltan Bridge in Ambala after a car allegedly driven by a drunk police officer rammed into an e-rickshaw and ran over her. The deceased has been identified as Nikita.

body.html:
Ambala (Haryana): A 22-year-old woman was killed in a tragic road accident near the Kali Paltan Bridge in Ambala after a car allegedly driven by a drunk police officer rammed into an e-rickshaw and ran over her.

The deceased has been identified as Nikita. According to eyewitnesses, the accused policeman was driving at high speed in a crowded area when he lost control of his vehicle and hit an e-rickshaw. The impact threw Nikita off the vehicle onto the road.

Witnesses alleged that instead of stopping, the policeman drove the car over the young woman, resulting in her death on the spot. Locals present at the scene overpowered the accused officer and handed him over to the police.

The incident triggered widespread outrage. Angry residents and family members staged a protest and created a ruckus at Ambala Civil Hospital late at night, demanding strict action against the accused.

Another eyewitness claimed that the policeman appeared to be under the influence of alcohol at the time of the accident and was driving recklessly despite heavy traffic in the area.

As of now, the police have refused to comment officially on the matter. An investigation is expected to determine the exact sequence of events and whether the accused officer was indeed intoxicated while driving.

The incident has sparked serious concerns over accountability and road safety, particularly involving law enforcement personnel.

#Ambala #Haryana #RoadAccident #DrunkDriving #PoliceNegligence #JusticeForNikita #KaliPaltanBridge #PublicOutrage
